doc.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Missing America: pine trees and French's mustard
summary: He missed pine trees and some American foods, and mentions being an Eagle Scout.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: What do you think — did you miss much of America when you went to Australia?

Yeah, for a long time I missed pine trees. Because I was a scout, you know. I mentioned the scouts marching by in the parade — I actually got up to be an Eagle Scout and so we went on lots of hikes and I spent a lot of time in the woods up around Lake Tahoe. And I love the forest. And in Australia they only have gum trees, you know, eucalyptus, which are different, they’re kind of scraggly trees. And I missed the pine trees a lot, and I still do. And some of the food that you can get in America, like French’s mustard, they don’t have that down there.
Yeah. It’s true. You get used to certain things when you’re growing up here. Not much else.
